newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore insurance rules raise sector's image.
newsitem.headline: Singapore insurance rules raise sector's image.

text.p: New rules controlling financial guarantee insurance in Singapore raise the standing of the sector, a senior executive told Reuters on Tuesday.

"They help to reinforce the image that this is a well-run business, tightly regulated, that stands up to scrutiny," Alex Lam, chief operating officer of ASIA Ltd, said of rules unveiled on Friday by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).
Financial guarantee insurers underwrite big infrastructure and infrastructure-funding projects.
Asian Securitization and Infrastructure Pte Ltd (ASIA Ltd) was the first such insurer set up in Singapore in May last year and industry sources expect a second to be launched soon.

Through its founding sponsors -- which include CapMac Holdings Inc, the Asian Development Bank and the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation -- ASIA Ltd had been liaising with MAS officials for two years to help draw up the new regulations, Lam said.

The new rules setting minimum paid-up capital requirements and claims paying ability ratings for companies entering the sector were detailed in the latest issue of the Government Gazette, the Straits Times newspaper said on Friday.
